question: what the 448-cell calibration null rules out, and its sensitivity to the grid and to the selection rule

provenance.per_cell_readings: verified by the owner in an isolated worktree against the sealed artifact, 2026-11-07; not recomputed in this worktree
provenance.artifact: docs/confirmation/calibration.json is on the owner's machine and is absent from this worktree
provenance.recomputable: grid, degrees, arms, cell count, derived sets, selection semantics

design.liveness: every one of the final 10% of cycles holds >= 1 theory and the tail mean beliefs >= 2
design.selection: highest mean coverage among taus that are live on every cell AND hold precision >= 0.95 on every cell; ties to the larger tau

ratio.at_or_above_0.20: precision is None in every cell: no stable predictions exist
ratio.below_0.20: not itemized in the summary; section 18 records that nothing qualified

reported_rejections.note: the transition rejections are the owner's verified readings of the sealed artifact; the ratio arm's per-cell pattern below 0.20 is unresolved

correction.cause: section 18's summary placed the transition precision boundary at 0.20 and did not report the degree-12 liveness rejection already at 0.15
correction.now: the untested interval is (0.10, 0.15), one grid step wide
correction.effect_on_reading: the resolution risk was understated. The two gates are rejected at adjacent thresholds for opposite reasons, so the only possible single-threshold solution lies inside that untested interval. Under monotone gates it exists if the precision crossing precedes the liveness crossing there; if it does, the null is a resolution artifact, and if it does not, the null is structural. The grid cannot tell the two apart.
correction.verdict: unchanged: no qualifying threshold on the grid, no held-out cell, nothing adopted

what_it_rules_out: a tau in the committed grid that is live on all 32 cells per arm and holds precision >= 0.95 on all 32
shipping either calibrated formula at a single global threshold, as tested
what_it_does_not_rule_out: a single global threshold inside the untested interval (0.10, 0.15)
a per-degree threshold (out of scope by section 3, not refuted)
a degree-aware or otherwise non-constant rule
the 0.95 floor relaxed, or precision pooled rather than required per cell
worlds, seeds, degrees or horizons outside the calibration design
anything about the held-out stage: no held-out cell exists
anything about the task endpoint: it was never measured at calibration
the mechanism: both arms died at the same stage
